packet.prompt:
Read only the supplied manuscript images. Do not search for the text, open a
catalogue or edition, or consult an earlier transcription. Do not identify the
work or author. If prior context has already revealed a proposed identification
or reading, stop and report that exposure instead of calling this a blind reading.

Begin with a brief image-only layout survey. Note orientation, columns, running
titles, rubrics, enlarged initials, underlined text, and interlinear or marginal
glosses when visible. Distinguish observations from tentative interpretations
such as main text with commentary. Do not infer author, work, date, or provenance.
A tight crop may not show the layout; say so rather than guessing.

Use those features to choose a few useful spans: headings or question openings,
then connecting prose, transitions or citation chains. Keep quoted lemmata and
commentary separate. Read enough surrounding prose to make a later source match
checkable; a full transcription is not required. State which areas you selected
and which remain unread. Suggest a wider view or an adjacent crop if needed.

Transcribe those spans, preserving physical lines. Label each line with its
image filename and a line number counted from the top of that image. Keep columns
and marginal additions separate. Note overlapping crops rather than treating
repeated lines as additional text.

Retain abbreviation marks when possible. Put proposed expansions in parentheses,
uncertain readings before a question mark, and unreadable text in [illegible].
Describe visible deletions and additions explicitly. Do not supply missing words
from what would make grammatical or philosophical sense. Leave uncertainty visible.

Return the reading as UTF-8 plain text. Include limitations (cropped lines, damage,
uncertain column order) in that same response. This is an unverified image reading.

text:
packet-17 - unverified image reading (blind; no identification seen in context)

LAYOUT SURVEY (from overviews image-001.jpg and image-003.jpg)
- Two faces of one small parchment scrap, c. 8 x 7.5 cm against the scale bar, each photographed on black with colour chart and ruler. image-002.jpg and image-004.jpg are the native-resolution views of the scrap (one per face, apparently).
- Face A (image-001): about 20 lines of a small, compressed, heavily abbreviated Gothic book hand (textualis/semi-cursive), single block visible; no column edge visible on either side, so the scrap is cut from inside a text column (left and right edges of the text are cut). A modern pencil shelfmark runs vertically along the right edge ("...Sch...Tag. 148(?)..."), observation only. Holes in the centre (worm/damage). Upper and lower edges ragged; text runs to both.
- Face B (image-003): about 20 lines of the same type of hand, heavily stained and with a large hole centre-left. Near the top left a blue (?) mark/initial or paragraph sign; near the bottom left a red-ink mark (rubricated initial or paragraph sign). Pencil shelfmark vertical along the left edge (the reverse of face A's right edge). No running title visible; crop too tight to tell column structure.
- Tentative: continuous prose, probably one column of a text written in a small scholastic hand. Not interpreting further.

FACE A - image-002.jpg (native view of face A; single tile, whole scrap)
Observations on image-002: left vertical ruling visible at x~120 with text starting just right of it (so this is the LEFT edge of a text column; left margin partly preserved). Right edge of text at ~x 930, with a blank strip beyond; text lines end roughly at a common line, so the right edge of the column may also be present (column c. 6 cm wide?) - tentative. 18-19 text lines. Interlinear additions (small letters above lines) are frequent in lines 1-2. Hand: very small, compressed Gothic with heavy suspension and Tironian/abbreviation marks: q with stroke (quod/quia), p with stroke (per/pro), 9 (con-/-us), ꝛ (-rum), superscript vowels. Ink brown-black. A faint blue mark near the hole at mid-right (line ~11-12, x~700), perhaps an offset or a paraph.
Crops made: crop-A1.jpg (lines 1-7), crop-A2.jpg (lines 6-12), crop-A3.jpg (lines 12-18), crop-A4.jpg (lines 17-19) - each 2x enlargements of image-002.

Face A, areas unread or largely unread: the centre of ll.5-12 (holes and staining), left starts of ll.18-19 (abrasion). Everything on this face is low-confidence; the hand is extremely compressed and abbreviated.

FACE B - image-004.jpg (native view of face B; single tile, whole scrap)
Observations on image-004: text block x~250-1020, about 21 lines; left margin with modern pencil "Stams, StA, Frag. 148v" (vertical; recorded as observation only). Line 1 has a blue-ink bracket/initial-like stroke over the 2nd-3rd word (x~370-460) - possibly a blue paraph or a small blue initial. Bottom left (ll.18-20, x~250-340) a red-outlined enlarged initial (with dark infill; letter form unclear) and a further reddish mark beside it. A red horizontal stroke/underline at right of l.16 (x~800-1000) - perhaps red line-filler or underlining. Heavy dark staining over the left-centre and centre, a large hole at ll.11-13 centre-left, abrasion at bottom centre and right. Same type of small abbreviated Gothic hand as face A.
Crops made: crop-B1.jpg (ll.1-8), crop-B2.jpg (ll.8-15), crop-B3.jpg (ll.15-20), crop-B4.jpg (ll.19-21), each 2x enlargements of image-004.

LIMITATIONS AND NOTES
- All readings are low confidence: a very small, densely abbreviated scholastic hand on a stained, holed scrap. Most words are given at letter level with suspensions kept; expansions are proposals only.
- Line numbers are physical lines counted from the top of image-002 (face A) and image-004 (face B). Crops overlap by about one line; overlapping lines are marked "(repeat)" and not counted twice.
- Which face is recto/verso: the pencil notes read "...148r"(?) on face A (last character unclear, could be "r") and "...148v" on face B; I record only what the pencil shows.
- Recurrent words that a matcher could test (all tentative): face A "figura/figuram", "ad vocem", "ad modum", "modus", "in proposito"; face B "significatione(m)", "in compositione", "ad vocem per modum", "adducere/adducit", "ad causam", "perfectum".
- Suggest: a raking-light or UV image of face B centre (stain) and higher-resolution capture would help; the native images here were enlarged 2x only.
- Exposure: nothing in my context revealed an identification. The pencil shelfmark visible on the images ("Stams, StA, Frag. 148...") was read from the images themselves. I did nothing beyond the brief: listed only the packet's image files, made 2x crops into the private scratch folder.
